questions.stem: A 70-year-old man on surgical high-dependency unit has been admitted with a 2-day history of vomiting and upper abdominal pain. He is hypotensive and hypovolaemic, has cool peripheries and increased capillary refill. His hypotension is being treated by increasing cardiac preload with a fluid challenge of 500 mL crystalloid solution. Which of the following most accurately describes this patient’s cardiac preload?
questions.explanation: The initial length of a cardiac myocyte determines its contractility. Preload reflects ventricular volume and hence myocyte length.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man on the surgical high-dependency unit has been complaining of chest pain for the past hour. Cardiac ischaemia is suspected since the patient has a history of angina and his ECG shows ST depression in the lateral leads. What is the main determinant of his coronary blood flow?
questions.explanation: The Hagen–Poiseuille equation describes laminar flow through tubes. The radius of coronary arteries has the greatest importance as flow is inversely proportional to the radius.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 58-year-old man on the postoperative surgical ward has hypotension. He underwent a laparoscopic cholecystectomy earlier today. The patient has a history of ischaemic heart disease. To treat the hypotension his cardiac output will be optimised. To increase cardiac output with least impact on myocardial oxygen demand which one of the following physiological variables should be optimised?
questions.explanation: Preload increases contractility but, because of the Laplace relationship, produces a much smaller increase in oxygen demand than the other factors.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 38-year-old woman underwent a laparoscopic biopsy of a vascular lesion. The biopsy results are being reviewed. On the histopathology report, there is no mention of the site of the biopsy, however, the biopsy is found to contain a large proportion of elastic tissue. Based on this report, where is the elastic tissue most likely to originate from?
questions.explanation: One of the key functions of the aorta is to maintain blood flow and pressure during diastole. This is dependent on the presence of a peripheral resistance and compliance.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 56-year-old man is being assessed for repair of a large aortic aneurysm. As part of his assessment he is going to undergo cardiopulmonary exercise testing. Which organ receives the greatest proportion of cardiac output before the start of the test?
questions.explanation: Regional blood flow is regulated by the arterioles which contain a large proportion of smooth muscle in their walls.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 65-year-old woman is on the surgical high-dependency unit in peri-arrest. Her heart rate is 30 beats per minute, her SpO₂ is 80% and the monitor is unable to measure a systolic blood pressure. High-flow oxygen and IV fluids are being administered. The house officer asks if IV adrenaline should be given. Which one of the following adrenoreceptors causes vasoconstriction by adrenaline?
questions.explanation: Adrenoreceptors exert their effects via intracellular secondary messenger systems. α₁-receptors increase smooth muscle contraction, including vasoconstriction.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition

questions.stem: A 21-year-old man is brought in by ambulance to the emergency department with an abdominal stab wound. He is in class 3 hypovolaemic shock and is being resuscitated by the emergency team. The carotid baroreceptors are some of the main sensors of intravascular volume status. What is the afferent nerve supply of the carotid baroreceptors?
questions.explanation: Carotid and aortic baroreceptors are stretch receptors that are stimulated by increased distension of the vessel wall. Decreased intra-arterial pressure causes less vessel wall stretch and hence reduced activation of the baroreceptors.
questions.source_label: MRCS Part A: 550 SBAs and EMQs || 2nd Edition
